full_judgment:
3. Both the suits were tried together; one set of evidence was led by the parties. Both the parties examined equal number of 5 witnesses and adduced number of documents. The trial Court dismissed both the suits on contest. Two appeals were preferred therefrom by both the parties. Title Appeal No. 57 of 1995 preferred by Kalimullah was allowed but Title Appeal No. 182 of 1994 taken by Fariduddin Ahmed was dismissed. The above Rules were obtained by Fariduddin Ahmed against those appellate judgment and decree. 

 4. Mr Nur Hussain Chowdhury, learned Advocate of the petitioners, submits that trial Court held that the deed of lease dated 18-5-65 as genuine and that the petitioner acquired title by said deed and also found the petitioner in possession of the suit land but due to some misconception dismissed the suit. On such merit of the case of the parties, the trial Court rightly dismissed the suit of Kalimullah. But in appeal the appellate Court without considering the entire evidence on record rather on misconception of law found the lease in question was not valid beyond five years and thereby, the petitioner acquired no valid title. In such wrong view of the matter the court of appeal below dismissed the suit of the petitioner and decreed the suit of opposite party No.1 

 7. With regard to possession, the trial Court appears to have considered the oral evidence and came to a finding that opposite party No.1 failed to prove his possession and that the petitioner was in possession in one part of his judgment but at the conclusion it held the possession of the petitioner was not definitely and clearly proved. Upon such view the trial Court dismissed the suit of the petitioner. Appellate Court appears to have considered no oral evidence at all. The conclusion of the appellate Court on possession is influenced by its wrong decision on the deed of lease. Such finding on possession based on total non-reading of the evidence, oral and documentary, on record cannot also be sustained in law. In the circumstances, impugned judgment and decree cannot be sustained in law. 

 8. In the result, both the Rules are made absolute. No costs, the impugned judgments and decrees are hereby set aside. Judgment and decree of the trial Court in Title Suit No. 26 of 1992 are restored and Title Suit No. 26 of 1992 is dismissed. Title Suit No. 38 of 1992 is sent back on remand to the trial Court for writing out a fresh judgment on the question of possession and dispossession only as made out by the petitioner Fariduddin Ahmed in the light of the observation as made hereinabove. The order of stay granted earlier is hereby re-called and vacated.
